Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

input.rationale: Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "early termination", and shortfall/termination-fee language return no provision requiring Customer to pay liquidated damages, a penalty, or a minimum fee on termination. The only "penalty" reference (§ 27.3) confirms Customer may terminate without penalty, which favors us. § 2.1's USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment creates volume exposure, but that is a minimum-commitment term addressed under MINCOMMIT and is not styled as liquidated damages or an early-termination charge, so it is not double-flagged here; § 7.1 further bars unidentified minimum-use charges. The document therefore meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), and no redline is proposed.

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us for three years expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — precisely the walk-away position under MINCOMMIT (multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right), and well short of the fallback (single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up rather than penalised). It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment, and § 7.1's prohibition on unidentified minimum-use charges. We therefore redline to the preferred position: no minimum commitment, with fees payable only for usage or ordered Services, and flag the 12-month/30-day-reduction true-up structure as the fallback if a commitment is commercially required.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year take-or-pay minimum; fees payable for usage or ordered Services only
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced it with payment for usage and ordered Services only — consistent with § 12.3, which already confirms we make no minimum-volume commitment. If Cobalt needs a commitment, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us for three years expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — precisely the walk-away position under MINCOMMIT (multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right), and well short of the fallback (single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up rather than penalised). It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment, and § 7.1's prohibition on unidentified minimum-use charges. We therefore redline to the preferred position: no minimum commitment, with fees payable only for usage or ordered Services, and flag the 12-month/30-day-reduction true-up structure as the fallback if a commitment is commercially required.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: compliant** (rule LD — liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer).

No customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee exists anywhere in the agreement; the only "penalty" reference (§ 27.3) is a customer-favorable right to terminate without penalty, and § 7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use charges. The § 2.1 take-or-pay commitment is volume exposure properly handled under the minimum-commitment rule, not a liquidated-damages clause, so it is not flagged twice here. This sits at the preferred position, so no redline was proposed.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "early termination", and shortfall/termination-fee language return no provision requiring Customer to pay liquidated damages, a penalty, or a minimum fee on termination. The only "penalty" reference (§ 27.3) confirms Customer may terminate without penalty, which favors us. § 2.1's USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment creates volume exposure, but that is a minimum-commitment term addressed under MINCOMMIT and is not styled as liquidated damages or an early-termination charge, so it is not double-flagged here; § 7.1 further bars unidentified minimum-use charges. The document therefore meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), and no redline is proposed.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.

Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Comment prefix: [Playbook].

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (§ 2.1, p0012)**

§ 2.1 binds us to a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay purchase commitment for three years, expressly "without reduction or termination rights." That is the walk-away position under MINCOMMIT and falls short of the fallback (a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty). It also sits inconsistently with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment, and with § 7.1's bar on unidentified minimum-use charges.

Redline (validated, preferred position): replace the commitment with "Customer has no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment. Customer is obligated to pay only for Services it actually uses or orders under an executed Order Form," offering the 12-month / 30-day reduction / true-up structure as a fallback if Cobalt needs a commitment.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
§ 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us for three years expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — precisely the walk-away position under MINCOMMIT (multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right), and well short of the fallback (single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up rather than penalised). It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment, and § 7.1's prohibition on unidentified minimum-use charges. We therefore redline to the preferred position: no minimum commitment, with fees payable only for usage or ordered Services, and flag the 12-month/30-day-reduction true-up structure as the fallback if a commitment is commercially required.

Original paragraphs:
p0012: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
p0044: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Rendered redline:
p0012: 2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment. Customer is obligated to pay only for Services it actually uses or orders under an executed Order Form.

Comment:
[Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced it with payment for usage and ordered Services only — consistent with § 12.3, which already confirms we make no minimum-volume commitment. If Cobalt needs a commitment, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised.

Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
input.rationale: Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) addresses only access wind-down, Deliverable delivery and Fee refunds. Section 10.1 refers to "any agreed transition period" but creates no transition-assistance obligation or period, and no provision anywhere obliges Vendor to return or export Customer Data in a usable format or to certify deletion: Section 16.5 covers only Confidential Information and expressly defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15", but Section 11 does not exist in the Agreement and Section 15 contains only processing-limitation and privacy-compliance terms. The rule's material elements (transition assistance period and data return within 30 days) therefore fail even the fallback, and the missing return obligation leaves us exposed to the walk-away scenario of no data return. Inserted new Section 10.3 at the preferred position (six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion), with 90 days offered as a fallback in the comment.

The current Section 10 covers access wind-down and Deliverables but says nothing about getting our data back or migration help; if six months is difficult we can work with 90 days of assistance.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: missing** (TRANSITION) — validated redline submitted.

The Agreement has no post-termination transition-assistance or data-return obligation:
- **§10.1** ends our access "after any agreed transition period" but never creates such a period or any assistance duty.
- **§10.2** covers only Deliverable delivery and Fee refunds.
- **§16.5** returns/destroys *Confidential Information* only and expressly defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15" — but **Section 11 does not exist** in the document, and Section 15 contains only processing-limitation and privacy terms with no return, export or deletion mechanic.

That gap fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance + 30-day export) and risks the walk-away outcome of no data return at all. I inserted a new **§10.3** at the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return/extraction of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter (subject to routine backups and legal retention, consistent with §16.5). The comment offers 90 days as a fallback if the six-month period is resisted.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing

Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of vendor-form Master Services Agreement
**Status:** All findings below are verified (verification: pass)

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and identified **10 issues** requiring action (7 deviations and 3 missing clauses) against **8 clauses that already meet our position**.

The commercial architecture of the draft is unbalanced in three ways:

- **The ri[REDACTED] package is incomplete.** There is no indemnification provision anywhere — the numbering jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and the absent Section 20 leaves dangling cross-references in Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5. There is also no termination-for-convenience right and no transition-assistance or data-return obligation. Each of these sits in walk-away territory, and we have inserted clauses at the preferred position.
- **Several one-way restrictions bind us rather than Vendor.** Section 2.1 (three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights), Section 7.2 (right of first refusal plus an MFN matching obligation running against us), and Section 12.4 (24-month post-term non-compete and 24-month no-hire) all fail the fallback on multiple material terms. Notably, each of these directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, minimum-volume, most-favoured-customer or no-hire commitment — so the redlines also cure internal inconsistency.
- **Ownership and forum are wrong.** Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for us with only a revocable, term-limited licence back, and Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts while Section 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the New York County courts.

On the positive side, the limitation of liability (Section 21), assignment and change of control (Section 24), licence grant (Section 13), audit rights (Section 22), renewal mechanics (Section 8), warranties (Section 19) and Vendor insurance (Section 18) all meet our preferred position, and there are no liquidated damages or termination penalties payable by us. Those clauses are not redlined.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 19.5 (gap where Section 20 should sit; cross-referenced at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4) |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4) |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 2.1 (see also §§ 7.1, 27.3) |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.3) |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 |
| 9 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 |
| 10 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (Termination) |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2–22.3) |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 (conflicts with § 28.2) |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Deviation | § 2.1 |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (see also § 16.5) |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and must be resolved before signature:

| Rule | Section | Why it is walk-away | Our position |
|---|---|---|---|
| INDEMN | Missing Section 20 | No Vendor IP indemnity at all; the absent Section 20.5 IP remedies are already cross-referenced in § 9.3 | Insert a new Section 20 at the preferred position: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; customary exclusions; procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (restoring § 20.5); notice, control and cooperation procedure; and a Customer indemnity narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. No super-cap needed because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims. |
| T4C | § 9 | No convenience exit for us in a three-year term, compounded by § 2.1's take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" | Insert a new § 9.4: Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, expressly overriding § 2.1, and confirm Vendor has no convenience right during a term. |
| MINCOMMIT | § 2.1 | Multi-year take-or-pay (USD 2,000,000/year for three years) with no reduction or termination right; contradicts §§ 12.3 and 7.1 | Remove the minimum commitment; fees payable for usage or ordered Services only. Fallback: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised. |
| EXCLUSIVITY | § 7.2 | De facto right of first refusal on our sourcing, with no service-category limit, no 12-month sunset and no performance-based exit; contradicts § 12.3 | Remove the exclusivity / first-refusal gate on engaging another provider. |
| MFN | § 7.2 | MFN runs the wrong way (against us) and is unbounded as to product line, time and comparison carve-outs; contradicts § 12.3 | Delete the disclose-and-match obligation imposed on Customer. |
| NONCOMPETE | § 12.4 | 24-month post-term non-compete, any competing product or service, any territory, and expressly bars acquisitions; contradicts § 12.3 | Delete. Fallback offered in comment: a narrowed restriction tied to a specific Vendor product if protection is genuinely needed. |
| NOSOLICIT | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month no-hire covering every Vendor employee, expressly overriding general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs; contradicts § 12.3 | Narrow to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, measured from the end of an individual's involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and the no-hire element deleted. |
| GOVLAW | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts — outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) — and inconsistent with § 28.2 | Replace with New York law and defer venue to the New York County courts already named in § 28.2. §§ 28.3 escalation and the interim-injunctive-relief carve-out are acceptable and left intact. |
| TRANSITION | § 10.1 | No obligation to return or export Customer Data in usable form; § 16.5 defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15", but Section 11 does not exist and Section 15 covers only processing limitations and privacy compliance | Insert new § 10.3: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, Customer Data return in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion. Fallback of 90 days' assistance offered in the comment. |

**Critical deviation outside the walk-away list.** § 14.2 (IP) gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for us (as defined in § 1.4), leaving us only a revocable, non-transferable licence for the Order Form term. That fails both the preferred position and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense), and the § 13.2 perpetual licence pulled in by § 14.3 does not cure it because it is limited to software and Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable. Our redline reverses ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment, while preserving Vendor's ownership of Vendor Technology under §§ 14.3/13.2. §§ 14.1 and 14.4 are satisfactory and unchanged.
